correctness.rationale: All 28 lines are explicitly proved bitangent in odd characteristic and exhaustive by the classical theta-characteristic count. The norm formula is derived algebraically. An exhaustive 3276-determinant stdlib certificate proves all new concurrences restricted to p=3,5,17; exhaustive pairwise-intersection enumerations in Fp^2 prove exact profiles for 3,5,17 and generic representative 7. The norm nonvanishing transfer closes the all-characteristics proof.

evidence: Knecht–Reyes, Theorems 4.1,4.5, concern individual finite fields; their §2 supplies general bitangent-incidence bounds, not an all-prime specialization theorem.
Janasz–Pokora–Zieliński, §3.2, is over the complex numbers and thus cannot decide accidental modular concurrence.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader theory of 28 theta characteristics ensures completeness of the line family but does not supply simultaneous arithmetic incidence specialization. The norm computation is necessary to rule out other exceptional primes.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A complex concurrence configuration does not imply reduction stability at all primes. Two known modular special cases do not imply an all-prime restriction or the p=5 exceptional triple locus. The final statement is the strengthened global reduction theorem, not any previously covered row alone.

originality.rationale: 2015 Knecht–Reyes already establishes Fermat incidence for p=3 and p=17; a later complex study covers p=0, and the small-field database includes some finite instances. They do not establish the uniform exceptional-prime classification or the new p=5 16 triple points; searches yielded no stronger covering claim. Residual uncatalogued literature risk is retained.
residual_risks: An uncatalogued arithmetic specialization paper could include the same all-prime characteristic-5 result; novelty is best-knowledge, not a uniqueness proof.
Online finite-field tables list individual fields; a full external compilation could contain an equivalent characteristic-five count not identified here.
